title: Oscars: Japan Selects ‘All of a Sudden’ for International Feature Race
description: Hamaguchi Ryusuke‘s “All of a Sudden” has been selected as Japan’s entry in the international feature category at the 99th Academy Awards, the Motio
body:
Hamaguchi Ryusuke‘s “All of a Sudden” has been selected as Japan’s entry in the international feature category at the 99th Academy Awards, the Motion Picture Producers Association of Japan (Eiren) has revealed.

	The selection marks the second time a Hamaguchi film has represented Japan in the category, five years after “Drive My Car” won the international feature Oscar and picked up nominations for best picture, director and adapted screenplay at the 94th Academy Awards.
	

	“All of a Sudden” is a France-Japan co-production made with backing from Germany and Belgium, shot largely in Paris. The film draws on “When Life Suddenly Takes a Turn: Twenty Letters Between a Philosopher With Terminal Cancer and a Medical Anthropologist,” a book of correspondence by Miyano Makiko and Isono Maho. It follows Marie-Lou Fontaine (Virginie Efira), who runs a nursing home outside Paris and pushes to adopt a more dignity-focused model of elderly care, and Morisaki Mari (Okamoto Tao), a Japanese theater director undergoing cancer treatment. Nagatsuka Kyōzō and Kurosaki Kōdai round out the cast.


	The film premiered in competition at the Cannes Film Festival in May, where it drew a seven-minute standing ovation. Efira and Okamoto shared the festival’s best actress prize; Okamoto is the first Japanese performer to win it.

	“All of a Sudden” opened in Japan on June 19 through Bitters End. Diaphana Distribution released the film in France on Aug. 12, and Neon will open it in North American theaters on Nov. 25.

	Eiren’s pick now advances to the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, which will winnow submissions from countries around the world down to a shortlist of 15 films before narrowing to five nominees. The 99th Academy Awards ceremony will take place March 14, 2027.

schema.headline: Oscars: Japan Selects ‘All of a Sudden’ for International Feature Race

title: Korea’s DRX Signs Strategic Partnership With Indonesia’s Nuon to Expand Gaming and Entertainment Ties (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Korea’s DRX Corp. and PT Nuon Digital Indonesia signed a strategic partnership in Jakarta to expand gaming and entertainment ties between Indonesia
body:
Korea’s DRX Corp. and PT Nuon Digital Indonesia signed a strategic partnership in Jakarta to expand gaming and entertainment ties between Indonesia and Korea, starting with an entertainment festival called DRX Homefront Indonesia and a joint game publishing initiative between the two countries.

	The agreement pairs DRX’s esports, content production and fan engagement experience with Nuon’s local distribution network, creator relationships and knowledge of the Indonesian market. The two companies plan to start by exploring three areas: live entertainment, game publishing and talent development.
	

	Indonesia’s population of more than 280 million, its mobile-first consumer base and its appetite for Korean entertainment make it a market both companies pointed to directly in unveiling the deal.


	“Indonesia is an important market for the future of entertainment in Asia,” said Can Yang, CEO of DRX. “Success in this market requires more than bringing an international brand to local audiences. It requires the right local knowledge, relationships and execution. Working with Nuon gives us the opportunity to develop experiences that reflect what Indonesian audiences want while creating stronger connections with Korea’s entertainment industry.”

	The companies will explore developing DRX Homefront Indonesia as a flagship festival in Jakarta built around gaming and entertainment, drawing in players, fans and creators from both countries. Plans on the table include competitive gaming showcases, community programs for creators, fan meet-ups and concert-style shows featuring K-pop acts.
	

	On the publishing side, the partnership will look at bringing select Korean game titles into Indonesia while helping Indonesian-developed games reach Korea. That would put DRX and Nuon in charge of everything from picking titles and adapting them for the local market to marketing, signing up players, getting the games into stores and handling payments.

	The companies also plan to bring pieces of DRX’s existing academy setup to Indonesia, with organized coaching, camps held in Korea and routes for Indonesian players to break into the region’s pro gaming circuit.

	“Indonesia’s growing gaming and digital entertainment ecosystem presents significant opportunities for collaboration with leading players from Korea,” said Chandra Tamrin, director of Nuon. “Through this partnership with DRX, we aim to connect the strengths of both markets – bringing new gaming and entertainment experiences to Indonesian audiences while creating pathways for Indonesian games, talent and creative opportunities to reach the Korean and broader regional market. This collaboration reflects our commitment to continuously expanding Indonesia’s digital entertainment ecosystem through international partnerships.”

	DRX and Nuon plan to form a joint team to map out their initial projects and how the rollout will work, with more specifics expected once those plans come together.

	The Nuon deal extends a broader push DRX has been making beyond its esports roots. The company recently detailed plans to move into K-dramas and game publishing through its subsidiary WebsCreative, including agreements around two unannounced, fully cast K-drama projects with major Korean broadcasters. Yang has described the goal as building DRX into a digital entertainment company that keeps esports as one pillar among several, with Southeast Asia named as a priority region for that growth – a strategy the Jakarta signing puts into practice.

schema.headline: Korea’s DRX Signs Strategic Partnership With Indonesia’s Nuon to Expand Gaming and Entertainment Ties (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘Heroes’ Stars Throw Reunion to ‘Celebrate the Life’ of Hayden Panettiere: ‘So Much Love, Gratitude and Warmth’
description:
The cast of “Heroes” got together to celebrate the life of their co-star Hayden Panettiere, who died on Aug. 16 at 36 years old.

	“A ‘HEROES’ reuni
body:
The cast of “Heroes” got together to celebrate the life of their co-star Hayden Panettiere, who died on Aug. 16 at 36 years old.

	“A ‘HEROES’ reunion to celebrate the life of HAYDEN was deeply emotional,” series star Jimmy Jean-Louis wrote on X, sharing photos of himself with his former castmates. “There was sadness in our hearts, but also so much love, gratitude and warmth as we remembered the beautiful moments shared and the lasting impact of a life that touched so many. Au revoir Hayden.”
	

	Panettiere’s death was announced via a statement from her father, Skip Panettiere, to ABC: “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden. She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her — and to the millions who watched her onscreen.”


	Several members of the “Heroes” family spoke out after news broke of Panettiere’s death. Jack Coleman, who played her father on the NBC drama, shared an emotional tribute on Instagram.

	“I’m heartbroken. I couldn’t begin to put my thoughts into words until now, and they will be inadequate,” Coleman wrote. “I’ve loved Hayden since day one of the pilot of ‘Heroes,’ 20 years ago, when she introduced herself by shouting ‘daddy’ and throwing her arms around me. From that day on, she called me daddio. She was Haydini, because she was a magician.”

	“Heroes” creator Tim Kring penned a guest essay for Variety about Panettiere after her death. In it, he wrote, “Hayden was a true team player, which was important for a show with a large ensemble cast. She was levelheaded beyond her years as a person and singularly talented as an actor, with an almost savant-like quality about her work. It wasn’t just that Hayden could learn lines with ease — it was her rare ability to find and explore the nuances of drama and humor and pathos in any scene she was in.”

schema.headline: ‘Heroes’ Stars Throw Reunion to ‘Celebrate the Life’ of Hayden Panettiere: ‘So Much Love, Gratitude and Warmth’

title: Vidio Teams With ReelShort for First Indonesian Short-Drama Partnership
description: Indonesian streaming platform Vidio has partnered with ReelShort, the microdrama platform owned by Crazy Maple Studio, marking ReelShort’s first ent
body:
Indonesian streaming platform Vidio has partnered with ReelShort, the microdrama platform owned by Crazy Maple Studio, marking ReelShort’s first entry into the Indonesian market. 

	Hundreds of ReelShort titles will become available on Vidio starting Sept. 1.

	The content will stream through a dedicated Short Drama tab, accessible to subscribers on Vidio’s TV Extra, Platinum, Platinum Extra and Ultimate packages. The catalog spans genres such as fantasy, family drama, romance and billionaire romance, told in episodes running 60-90 seconds. More than 200 titles will launch with Indonesian dubbing, with a wider slate available in Indonesian subtitles.
	

	Beyond distribution, the deal includes a co-production slate between ReelShort and Indonesian production houses, with resulting series set to appear on both platforms. The partnership is also framed as a skills exchange, giving Indonesian creative talent exposure to ReelShort’s production pipeline. The agreement was brokered by AR Global Media Network.


	The Vidio tie-up extends ReelShort’s Southeast Asian expansion after earlier partnerships in Thailand with AIS and in the Philippines with Globe. According to Media Partners Asia (MPA), ReelShort holds an estimated 29% share of global short-form drama revenue.

	Vidio’s Short Drama section has existed on the platform since last year. Vidio closed the second quarter of 2026 with 5.8 million paying subscribers in Southeast Asia, the third-largest total in the region. MPA data cited identifies Indonesia as Asia-Pacific’s biggest market for short-form drama viewership, representing 39% of the region’s audience, while mobile ad company Mintegral has recorded quarterly growth of 50%-200% for short-form drama apps since the third quarter of 2023.
	

	“Vidio continues to evolve alongside the changing ways Indonesians consume entertainment,” said Sutanto Hartono, CEO of Vidio. “As audiences increasingly look for content that fits seamlessly into their daily lives, we want to ensure they can find every type of entertainment they love on a single platform, from live sports, local originals, global entertainment to now, the rapidly growing format of short dramas. Our partnership with ReelShort not only responds to this emerging audience demand but also strengthens Vidio’s position as Indonesia’s most comprehensive entertainment platform, offering more choice, greater convenience, and an even richer viewing experience for our subscribers.”

	Crazy Maple Studio founder and CEO Joey Jia called the deal a milestone for the company’s regional strategy, saying it reflects a shift in how audiences consume entertainment as microdramas move toward the mainstream. “Indonesia is one of the region’s most dynamic entertainment markets,” Jia said. “We see tremendous potential not only to expand access to our global catalogue, but also to create original stories for Indonesian audiences. Through our planned local productions with Vidio and Indonesian production partners, we look forward to combining ReelShort’s global experience in developing high-performing short-drama IP with local creative talent to build stories and franchises that resonate locally while reaching audiences across the region and beyond.”

	Vidio’s move builds on its existing lead in Indonesia’s subscription video market. Per the MPA and AMPD Online Video Consumer Insights: Southeast Asia Q2 2026 report, Vidio holds the largest share of Indonesia’s SVOD subscriptions, at 20.7%.

	MPA CEO and executive director Vivek Couto pointed to that scale as central to Vidio’s standing in a crowded field. “Indonesia is one of the most competitive streaming markets in Southeast Asia, with strong demand for both local and international content,” Couto said. “Vidio’s position as the platform with the largest share of SVOD subscriptions in Indonesia, at 20.7%, reflects its ability to build scale through a deep understanding of the local market, supported by strong local content and engagement across categories. This position also highlights the increasingly important role of local platforms in shaping the streaming landscape across Southeast Asia.”
	

	Thousands of ReelShort episodes will be accessible on Vidio’s Short Drama tab starting Sept. 1.

schema.headline: Vidio Teams With ReelShort for First Indonesian Short-Drama Partnership

title: Google DeepMind, Amazon Web Services, Kling AI Join Busan Market Tech Program InnoAsia
description: The Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM), the market of the Busan International Film Festival, will present InnoAsia 2026, its program built around t
body:
The Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM), the market of the Busan International Film Festival, will present InnoAsia 2026, its program built around the intersection of film and emerging technology. 

	This year’s participants include Amazon Web Services (AWS), Kling AI, Google DeepMind and Alibaba Group, alongside a range of other technology and content companies and startups. The program is built around a vision of cinema and technology developing side by side, with a scope that runs from brand-film partnerships to the fast-growing microdrama business.
	

	ACFM and global marketing agency Innocean will co-host Cinema by Brand 2026, a new competition with the Producers Guild of Korea handling selection and production oversight. The platform links brand clients with filmmakers around the world to turn advertising messages into standalone films with real narrative ambition, rather than conventional commercials. This year’s contest calls for 20-minute short films built around Hanwha Group’s “Space Solar Power.” First-round picks arrive in early September, followed by final pitching later that month, with winners named during ACFM. Selected teams get production funding and will see their films shown to audiences in Korea and abroad. A market session will dig into what branded content means for the business and how the initiative came together, with participation expected from Hanwha, Innocean and the selected directors.


	Beyond brands and filmmakers, InnoAsia is deepening ties with technology firms and international markets. This year’s AI-driven tech participants include AWS, Google DeepMind, BytePlus, Alibaba Cloud, Netflix’s VFX studio Eyeline Studios, MegazoneCloud, OPIM Digital, the Korean Film Archive’s VFX trading platform i.AM, Kling AI and Inshorts. 
	

	On the content-production side, France’s Atlas V joins Korea’s Mateo AI Studio, MBC C&I, Climax Studio, For Entertainment, K-Dragon and MooAm, while microdrama platforms Mango TV, FlickReels and Vigloo round out the roster. Kling AI will co-host two sessions with ACFM, New Cinematic Possibilities: Reimagining Filmmaking with Kling AI and a networking reception tied to production needs across Asia. AWS and MegazoneCloud will launch new AWS Awards linked to startup pitching, with winners chosen through a proof-of-concept process and awarded AWS cloud vouchers. On the international side, EFM-linked startup Lux AI, which builds intelligent lighting tools for virtual production, will travel to Busan along with Tanja Meissner, director of Berlinale Pro and EFM. Through a partnership with TAICCA School under the Taiwan Creative Content Agency, VFX-efficiency startup imCore will also take part.

	Seven Korean startups were chosen through an open call run with the Busan Center for Creative Economy & Innovation and AWS, together spanning the full content pipeline. On the development and production side, Lumicraft’s AI casting tool Castlink pairs actor discovery with contracting and settlement, while Reproduction’s Pre-Flow handles screenplay analysis and production data sharing. For localization, Voithru’s Totus offers AI dubbing across 29 languages, and XL8 brings both MediaCAT and EventCAT for video localization and real-time interpretation. On the exhibition side, Digion Cinema will show off an online cinema platform and AR smart glasses built for film viewing. MyStarChain will present its blockchain voting platform MyStarPick, and HiStranger will introduce Insight Flow, a tool that reads biosignals to gauge audience emotional response.

	InnoAsia 2026 will run several programs across three tracks: technology proof-of-concept and investment, creators and production, and industry and policy. The InnoAsia Startup Demo Jam sits at the center of the first track, with nine companies, drawn from the open call and international partner recommendations, pitching AI, virtual production and digital-asset technologies to investors and buyers. The InnoAsia WIP Showcase will preview AI-based features, animation, series and interactive projects from directors including Pierre Zandrowicz, Mark Wachholz and Kang Yunsung, paired with a colloquium on AI production pipelines. 
	

	A Cinematic AI conference will spotlight Google DeepMind’s AI animation work and an AI film from director Darren Aronofsky, both previously featured at Cannes Next, and will examine AI filmmaking ecosystems with input from Alibaba Cloud and Kling AI. AI Creators Camp offers hands-on workshops led by VFX supervisors from major studios and creators who have won at AI film festivals. On the policy side, a panel titled Microdrama – Data, AI, Formats and Audiences: China and Beyond brings together executives from Mango TV, FlickReels and Vigloo to discuss the $18 billion shortdrama market, while Next Foundation gathers voices from technology, policy and academia, including the National IT Industry Promotion Agency, to weigh questions around independent AI foundation models, AI assets, and IP and copyright in an era of AI transformation.

	InnoAsia 2026 will run Oct. 10-13, at Exhibition Center 2, BEXCO in Busan, alongside the 31st Busan International Film Festival, which runs Oct. 6-15, and the 21st Asian Contents & Film Market, held Oct. 10-13.

schema.headline: Google DeepMind, Amazon Web Services, Kling AI Join Busan Market Tech Program InnoAsia

title: Netflix’ Latest Marketing Mash-Up Pairs Stella Artois With ‘The Gentlemen’
description:
Netflix has what looks to be a great show set to launch, but you can’t see the program on its flagship streaming service.

	The company plans to tak
body:
Netflix has what looks to be a great show set to launch, but you can’t see the program on its flagship streaming service.

	The company plans to take over the history Marlborough Pub in London between September 3 and September 5, when it will outfit the place much like its comedic action series “The Gentlemen,” which is about to launch its second season. At the pub, visitors will be able to look for hidden messages from the show, which is created by Guy Ritchie, order a Stella Artois, and take home limited-edition merchandise including their an engraved chalice.
	

	The partnership, which will also include a series of vignettes outlining a five-step pouring ritual associated with the Anheuser-Busch InBev brew, marks the first brand alliance for the series, and the first execution in a multi-year deal struck between the brewing giant and the streaming titan, initially unveiled in September of last year.


	Wrapping Stella Artois in the trappings of the series was key to the alliance, says Marcel Marcondes, global CMO of Anheuser Busch InBev, via email. “We didn’t want to place the brand alongside the story,” he says. “We wanted to it feel so integrated that fans wouldn’t be able to distinguish between the content and the show.”

	The video vignettes will feature series star Theo James as well as soccer great David Beckham, who has served as a brand ambassador for the beer since 2024.

	Netflix has worked assiduously to burnish its reputation as a home for advertisers seeking to align themselves with its popular programs and eager to avoid the traditional model of deploying typical 30-second commercials.  Netflix in 2019 was able to convince Coca-Cola to revive New Coke, a failed revamp of its flagship product — all because the beverage was featured in the third season of “Stranger Things.” The streamer has put a spotlight on its ability to create bespoke alliances with its programs, according to media buyers who have negotiated ad deals with the company, realizing that such offerings might entice advertisers to buy more regular commercial inventory. Earlier this year, Netflix pushed the marketing-industry envelope by weaving popular State Farm spokes-character Jake from State Farm into the plot of its sports series “Running Point.”
	

	“We’re really excited about how this partnership came to life. It’s a true piece of entertainment that extends ‘The Gentlemen’ beyond the screen, that we know fans around the world are going to love,” says Magno Herran, vice president of global brand and marketing partnerships at Netflix, via email. “‘The Gentlemen; checks all the right boxes,” he adds. “It’s a show that our fans love globally, with a touch of real British style and swagger that pairs incredibly well with a brand like Stella Artois. It offered the perfect place for a brand and the story to come together in a way we couldn’t do individually.”

	The team-up between brewer and streamer will be seen in the U.S., the U.K., Canada, Brazil, Colombia, Mexico, South Africa and South Korea. The bet is that the interesting content will entice fans around the world and grow the series’ audience as the debut of its second season draws near. Social-media feeds controlled by Netflix or Stella Artois will also boost the alliance.

schema.headline: Netflix’ Latest Marketing Mash-Up Pairs Stella Artois With ‘The Gentlemen’

title: Amanda Kernell Is More Interested in ‘Liberation Than a Curse’ as Her Third Feature ‘Brace Your Heart’ Debuts Trailer (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
In her upcoming third feature “Brace Your Heart,” Amanda Kernell follows a survivor, not a victim. 

	“We’re all different, and some people who expe
body:
In her upcoming third feature “Brace Your Heart,” Amanda Kernell follows a survivor, not a victim. 

	“We’re all different, and some people who experience really difficult things can’t recover. But there are others who survive and find there’s light on the other side,” she told Variety. 

	Kernell, known for “Sámi Blood” and “Charter,” is also behind the script. 


	In the story, Ejva inherits her father’s reindeer herd following his sudden death. She must grow up, quickly, with only the local leader Heaika eager to help. However, Heaika expects some things in return and isn’t happy to see Ejva fall for his cousin. 
	

	The highly anticipated film is set to premiere at Toronto and San Sebastián. It debuts its exclusive trailer here:



	In 2023, Kernell won the top award at the Co-Production Market at Haugesund’s New Nordic Films industry sidebar for the film, which was then known as “The Curse: A Love Story.” 

	“After the curse of your own silence, or the curse that doesn’t allow you to speak up because you’re afraid of how people will think of you if you confront them,” she explained. 

	“Then I realized: OK. I’m more interested in liberation than a curse.”

	Sold by TrustNordisk, it’s produced by Eva Åkergren for Nordisk Film Production, and co-produced by Forest People, Compass Films, Invictus, Nordisk Film Production Denmark, Filmpool Nord, SVT and Film i Väst.

	Elli Sara Valkeapää plays Ejva. She’s joined by Andte Gaup-Juuso and Vincent Niia.
	

	“During casting, [Elli Sara Valkeapää] had just turned 18. I was like: ‘This is her. This is the girl I’ve written about.’ But that meant I had to change the whole film, because she speaks another Sámi language than I do,” explained Kernell. 

	“I have a Sámi father and a Swedish mother, and born in a village outside of Umeå I grew up surrounded by many strong, tough women. As a child, I admired them, and I also feared them a little bit,” she said. 

	“It seemed like they could survive anything, and maybe they had to. In this community, you have a responsibility greater than yourself.”

	Just like Ejva, who suddenly needs to learn how to protect the herd and make her family proud, even when a violent attack leaves her struggling.

	“This line from the title… It’s something you say to young Sámi people who are reindeer herders. You need to make your heart harder in order to survive,” she said. 

	“Maybe that’s how you get through difficult things and traumas and death – and a life that’s very close to death. But it’s not the path to love.”

schema.headline: Amanda Kernell Is More Interested in ‘Liberation Than a Curse’ as Her Third Feature ‘Brace Your Heart’ Debuts Trailer (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Motherhood Horror Film ‘Vagina Dentata,’ ‘From The Eclipse’ Director Nataša Urban, Boarded by Romanian Partner Manifest Film (EXCLUSIVE)
description: “Vagina Dentata,” the new film from Norwegian filmmaker Nataša Urban, whose “The Eclipse” won top honors at CPH:DOX in 2022, has been boarded by Man
body:
“Vagina Dentata,” the new film from Norwegian filmmaker Nataša Urban, whose “The Eclipse” won top honors at CPH:DOX in 2022, has been boarded by Manifest Film.

	The Romanian outfit will co-produce “Vagina Dentata,” a genre-bending exploration of motherhood and postnatal depression that will be pitched at this week’s Nordic Co-Production Market in Haugesund.

	Produced by Ingvil Giske through Norway’s Medieoperatørene, the project is currently 60% financed, with most of the secured funding coming from the Norwegian Film Institute. 
	

	In another addition to the film, Romanian editor Dana Bunescu — whose credits include Cristian Mungiu’s “4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days,” Cristi Puiu’s “The Death of Mr. Lăzărescu,” Călin Peter Netzer’s “Child’s Pose” and Alexander Nanau’s Oscar-nominated documentary “Collective” — is attached to edit.


	The team is now seeking additional co-production partners in France, Germany and/or Hungary, alongside further financing, distribution and festival connections. 

	“Vagina Dentata” is one of 21 projects being presented at the Nordic Co-Production Market, part of New Nordic Films during the Norwegian International Film Festival in Haugesund, which runs this week.

	Urban said the film was born out of the gap between cultural expectations surrounding motherhood and her own experience after becoming a parent.

	“When I became a mother, what I experienced was in no way what I had been told it would be like. Instead of sunshine and butterflies, all I could think about was death,” she said. “I was terrified — a feeling that is the baseline and driving force of this film, one that I hope many others will recognize.”
	

	The project uses horror and darkly comic genre elements to approach the psychological pressures of motherhood, extending Urban’s interest in personal experience as a route into broader social and political terrain.

	For Giske, “Vagina Dentata” also marks another collaboration with Urban after their previous work together.

	“It is such a pleasure working with Nataša again, her films are both wild, funny, serious and beautiful,” Giske said. “I feel there is a need to get more diverse stories about motherhood and Haugesund as a relatively small venue is the perfect place to meet with potential collaborators.”

	Giske added that previous trips to Haugesund had produced partnerships the company had not originally anticipated. “Last time I was here, we set up a co-production with a country I did not initially intend to work with, so I am really looking forward to seeing what will happen this time.”

	The Nordic Co-Production Market brings together Nordic and international producers, financiers, distributors and sales agents around projects in development.

	For “Vagina Dentata,” the immediate goal is to use the market to close the remaining financing and expand the project’s European co-production structure ahead of production.

schema.headline: Motherhood Horror Film ‘Vagina Dentata,’ ‘From The Eclipse’ Director Nataša Urban, Boarded by Romanian Partner Manifest Film (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Taylor Swift Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton: ‘She Was True Grace and True Grit, All in One Dazzling Person’
description:
Taylor Swift shared a touching tribute to the late Dolly Parton after the iconic singer-songwriter’s death on Tuesday.

	“A world without Dolly does
body:
Taylor Swift shared a touching tribute to the late Dolly Parton after the iconic singer-songwriter’s death on Tuesday.

	“A world without Dolly doesn’t feel possible, real, or right,” it reads. “But because of the eternally generous way she spent her time on this earth and the countless lives she changed for the better, her legacy will be an everlasting one. 

	“She was truly the gift that kept on giving. Dolly gave us someone to look up to while encouraging us to be who we are as individuals. Somehow she was able to give us her lessons about the world gently and honestly, simultaneously, and oftentimes hilariously. She managed to give the world the ultimate mystery and fantasy in some corners of her life, but to give full transparency in the ways that counted. Somehow she was true grace and true grit, all in one dazzling person. She possessed the softest heart when it came to the struggles of others, and a backbone of steel to defend her own self worth as an artist. 
	

	“Along with her other fans, I am so grateful for all of it. For the melodies and lyrics she wrote that thawed even the coldest hearts. For the millions of books she provided children all over the world so that they might fall in love with stories the way she did. For the tightropes she walked so that young girls like me could grow up dreaming of joining the circus too. 

	“Dolly, I’ll think of you each step of the way.”

	~ Taylor Swift 

	Parton, the queen of country music, died at age 80 in Nashville. Swift, who got her start in country music before going on to massive crossover success, has never been shy about her reverence for Parton, whom she recently described [via The Hollywood Reporter] as a “force of evolution and transformation” in the music business and a “storyteller for the ages.”
	

	Likewise, Parton has championed Swift, telling Variety that the younger songstress was “amazing” for what she’d accomplished in her career thus far.

	“I just admire her very much and how she’s handled her business, her personal life, and what all she has meant to so many young people,” Parton said in the 2024 interview. “[She’s] been a great inspiration. And Lord knows we need some uplifting people and things this day and time.”

	Last month, Parton posted a video message thanking Swift and Travis Kelce for donating $2 million to Parton’s Imagination Library (a literacy program that gifts free books every month to children from birth to age 5) ahead of their July 3 wedding at Madison Square Garden.

	“It’s evident that you two have made giving back a key part of your lives, so hey, when you have your firstborn, can I have it? Because that is going to be one special baby,” Parton joked, telling the couple she was “overjoyed” by their generosity and signing off by singing “I Will Always Love You.”

schema.headline: Taylor Swift Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton: ‘She Was True Grace and True Grit, All in One Dazzling Person’

title: LevelK Boards Haugesund-Bound Norwegian Psycho Thriller ‘Anathema,’ About Repression, Denial and Collective Madness (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Copenhagen-based sales and aggregation outlet LevelK has boarded the Norwegian psycho-thriller “Anathema” by promising directing duo Ea Johanne Sand
body:
Copenhagen-based sales and aggregation outlet LevelK has boarded the Norwegian psycho-thriller “Anathema” by promising directing duo Ea Johanne Sandberg and Alpha Nord.

	One of 21 projects in development to be pitched today at the Nordic Co-Production Market in Haugesund, “Anathema” is being shepherded by the seasoned Janne Hjeltnes (Netflix’s “Royalteen,” “Midsummer Night”) and Anne Borgaard Sørensen (“Camino”, “Bullshit”), also credited respectively as producer and executive producer of the Venice-bound “No Paradise If You Are Killed by a Woman.”
	

	Penned by Sandberg and Nord, “Anathema” is billed as a “visceral, unsettling exploration of repression, denial and collective madness.” The central character Dafne, lives in a valley with her mother and Bror. When he vanishes, she begins to question if she or her community is falling apart. His eventual return, drowned and dead, pushes the town into full‑scale delusion: no one admits his zombie-like state and everyone insists on celebrating his wedding, even if it means sacrificing his fiancée.


	“Dafne combines the truth-telling clarity of the boy in “The Emperor’s New Clothes” with the reluctant awakening of Neo in “The Matrix,” said the co-directors whose graduation short “Liminal Space” was selected for the New York City Independent Film Festival in 2025.

	“What excited us about the project was the fresh take on a known genre and the guts of the two young female directors to approach taboo subjects in an unconventional manner and thereby mark their debut with a clear ‘what the f***’ film which will have people do a double take,” commented Natascha Degnova, LevelK’s head of PR and marketing. She added: “This is the kind of project that fits very well into our strategy of including more genre titles to our slate, as well as of getting involved in projects before production, having a full journey and collaboration with the filmmakers from script to worldwide release.”
	

	“Anathema” is also the first feature under Hjeltnes and Sørensen’s banner Empathitude Pictures, set up in 2025 between Oslo and Copenhagen. “It’s exactly the kind of film we want to champion: character-driven, boundary-pushing and emotionally resonant, with a strong creative vision at its core,” said the producers, adding: “What makes the project particularly exciting to us is that it represents an extraordinary Gen Z approach to storytelling and filmmaking: instinctive, genre-fluid and unafraid of breaking with convention. It is the kind of filmmaking that does not simply work within an existing cinematic language but actively pushes it forward and expands what contemporary cinema can be.”

	The project’s film financing is being structured so far as a three-way co-production between Empathitude Pictures in Norway and Denmark and Junafilm in Germany, with funding from the Norwegian Film Institute. “It’s a low budget film [around $1.7 million] but it needs the right partners as we want those trailblazing Gen Z filmmakers to fulfil their vision,” the former Viaplay and The Global Ensemble Drama top executive Sørensen told Variety.

	At the Norwegian Film Festival’s industry sidebar New Nordic Films, currently underway, the Empathitude Pictures co-heads are looking for further co-financiers and distributors for “Anathema” and for their overall film and series slate.

	“With Anne, since launching Empathitude Pictures, we’ve been working relentlessly on our development slate, which was awarded Creative Media support this summer, so it feels like we have taken some good choices. Starting a new company these days is not easy, but we’re optimistic,” offered Hjeltnes who’s also thrilled to attend the Venice Film Festival with the world premiere – out of competition – of Halkawt Mustafa’s “No Paradise if You Are Killed by a Woman,” produced by Hene Films.  

	“I have been a producer alongside Halkawt for a decade, having produced as well his previous film “Hiding Saddam Hussein” [an IDFA world premiere in 2023]. “This is a dream come true,” she said.New Nordic Films closes Aug. 27 and the Norwegian Intl. Film Festival in Haugesund on Aug. 28.

schema.headline: LevelK Boards Haugesund-Bound Norwegian Psycho Thriller ‘Anathema,’ About Repression, Denial and Collective Madness (EXCLUSIVE)

                          After Casino's Lifetime Ban

            Former boxer Adrien Broner is facing a criminal trespass charge after cops say she showed up at a Florida casino despite being banned for life ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            According to court documents, Adrien is charged with trespass in connection with an alleged incident at the Seminole Hard Rock Hotel and Casino.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The Seminole Police Department report says officers were called to the casino in April 2024 over an alleged trespass. They say Adrien was issued a lifetime ban from the casino back in August 2023 ... but claim he came back anyway, leading to his arrest.
      

            The case has apparently dragged on for years … and recently the court issued a warrant for Adrien's arrest.
      
    
            Adrien has yet to respond to the case.
      
    
            As TMZ first reported, Adrien is facing an unrelated civil lawsuit brought by an alleged sexual assault victim. The boxer adamantly denies the accusations.

title: Beyoncé Honors Dolly Parton With Heartfelt Tribute on Her Website
description:
Dolly Parton
                          Beyoncé Calls Late Singer the "North Star" in Tribute
body:
Dolly Parton
                          Beyoncé Calls Late Singer the "North Star" in Tribute
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 25, 2026
                            7:54 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Beyoncé is paying emotional tribute to Dolly Parton ... honoring the late country icon as “the north star” who showed generations how to be unapologetically themselves.
      
    
            The “Cowboy Carter” singer posted a powerful message to her website Tuesday, remembering Dolly as “bold and brilliant” ... while thanking her for the massive impact she made through her music, philanthropy, humor and business savvy.
      
    
      
      Beyoncé pays tribute to the legendary Miss Dolly Parton. ❤️https://t.co/NysKafJI1N pic.twitter.com/zYv4UeHs6y
              @BeyLegion
          
  
    
            “Dolly, you were the barometer. The north star,” Beyoncé wrote … adding, “You taught so many lessons on how to be uniquely oneself.”
      

            Beyoncé and Dolly famously worked together on Bey’s 2024 “Cowboy Carter” album, with Dolly making a memorable appearance on the record and introducing Beyoncé’s reimagined version of “Jolene.”
      
    
            Bey said she’ll always treasure getting the chance to collaborate with Dolly ... writing, “Thank you for your profound impact on the world. You are an angel who has made this world a happier place because of your joyful art. You are truly one of one. Rest peacefully.”
      
    
            As we reported, Dolly died Tuesday at 80 following a brief battle with cancer. Her reps told us she was surrounded by loved ones at Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center in Nashville.
      
    
      
        
              
    
    
            Beyoncé joins a long list of stars honoring Dolly, including Reba McEntire, Jane Fonda, Kacey Musgraves and Sabrina Carpenter ... all sharing memories and celebrating the one-of-a-kind entertainer’s enormous heart and legacy.
